ip_top_stories.title: Machines with the ability to 'feel' currently in development as we enter next frontier of AI - Taylor & Francis Newsroom
ip_top_stories.summary: Taylor & Francis's newsroom covers the emerging development of AI systems capable of simulated feeling, marking a new frontier in artificial intelligence research. The piece reflects the publisher's ongoing engagement with AI developments relevant to academic and scientific publishing. As a Taylor & Francis story, it is prioritised per editorial policy.

ip_top_stories.title: Major publishers sue Meta for copyright infringement over AI training
ip_top_stories.summary: A group of major publishing houses have filed a lawsuit against Meta alleging copyright infringement in the use of books to train its AI systems, with publishers further alleging that Mark Zuckerberg personally authorised the use of pirated material. The case centres on claims that Meta knowingly used illegally obtained books as training data. Multiple outlets have covered the story; this version is selected as the primary report.

ip_top_stories.title: Association of American Publishers addresses AI, copyright and freedom of speech at AGM
ip_top_stories.summary: The Association of American Publishers used its annual general meeting to address the intersection of AI, copyright law, and freedom of speech, reflecting the publishing industry's growing focus on protecting intellectual property in the age of generative AI. The AAP's public stance signals continued industry-level advocacy on these issues.

ip_top_stories.title: Suno opposes disclosure of Warner Music deal in AI copyright case - Music In Africa
ip_top_stories.summary: AI music generation company Suno is resisting efforts to disclose the terms of Warner Music's licensing deal in an ongoing AI copyright case, raising questions about transparency in AI licensing agreements. The dispute highlights tensions between licensing confidentiality and the need for legal clarity in AI copyright litigation.

ip_top_stories.title: Copyright Office Sued Over Rejection Of AI 'Starry Night' Art
ip_top_stories.summary: A lawsuit has been filed against the US Copyright Office following its rejection of a copyright application for an AI-generated artwork styled after Van Gogh's 'Starry Night'. The case could have significant implications for the copyrightability of AI-generated creative works in the United States.

ip_further_links.title: AI Copyright Washing: How Metadata is Erased in Seconds
ip_further_links.summary: A report examines how AI tools can strip or alter copyright metadata from creative works almost instantaneously, raising serious concerns about rights management and attribution in the digital age.

ip_further_links.title: India opens AI copyright debate, proposes 'One Nation, One License' framework for training data
ip_further_links.summary: India has entered the global AI copyright debate by proposing a unified national licensing framework for AI training data, which could significantly affect how AI companies access copyrighted material in the country.

ip_further_links.title: AI licensing could drive new music royalties if rules are clear - Music In Africa
ip_further_links.summary: Industry analysis suggests that clear regulatory frameworks around AI licensing could open up new royalty streams for music rights holders, but ambiguity in current rules remains a barrier.

ip_further_links.title: IP's Real Legal Frontier With AI Is Everything Before the Output
ip_further_links.summary: A legal analysis argues that the most significant and underexplored intellectual property questions in AI concern the processes of data ingestion and model training, not just the final generated outputs.

ip_further_links.title: Creative Industries Unite to Defend Copyright in AI Age
ip_further_links.summary: A coalition of creative industry groups has issued a joint statement calling for stronger copyright protections in response to the growing use of creative works to train generative AI systems.

ip_further_links.title: Korea Music Copyright Association Restructures for AI Era
ip_further_links.summary: South Korea's Music Copyright Association has announced a structural reorganisation to better address the challenges and opportunities posed by AI, including establishing a dedicated AI oversight function.

ip_further_links.title: Beyond Copyright: Is Canada Ready to Protect Our Faces and Voices in the Age of Generative AI?
ip_further_links.summary: A Canadian legal commentary examines whether existing intellectual property frameworks are sufficient to protect individuals' likenesses and voices from being replicated by generative AI, suggesting new legislation may be needed.

ip_further_links.title: AAP Honors America's 250th at Annual Meeting [Metered]
ip_further_links.summary: Publishers Weekly reports on the Association of American Publishers' annual meeting, where AI, copyright, and the state of the publishing industry were among the topics discussed alongside the US semiquincentennial.

ip_further_links.title: AI Is Rapidly Accelerating Book Publishing, Says a16z
ip_further_links.summary: Venture capital firm Andreessen Horowitz argues that AI tools are significantly speeding up the book publishing process, with implications for authors, publishers, and the broader creative economy.

ip_further_links.title: HarperCollins Has a 'Heated' Quarter [Metered]
ip_further_links.summary: Publishers Weekly reports on HarperCollins's latest financial results, describing a turbulent quarter amid broader industry pressures including the impact of AI on publishing.
